headline_marked: 1,938 iPhones seized: [[6 Chinese nationals arrested]] in Cox's Bazar
headline: 1,938 iPhones seized: 6 Chinese nationals arrested in Cox's Bazar
summary: Police raided a hotel on the Marine Drive road, uncovering a massive haul of smartphones and laptops allegedly used for online scams.
details: Police arrested six Chinese nationals from the Hotel Sea Palace in Cox's Bazar after a raid conducted between Thursday night and Friday morning.
The operation recovered 1,938 iPhones, 40 laptops, and various communication tools, including equipment reportedly used by foreign police.
The arrests followed a tip-off from Dhaka police and a complaint filed at the Ramu police station regarding online-based fraud.
According to Ramu Police Station OC A K Fazlul Haque, the suspects were booked under the Cyber Security Act for their alleged involvement in online scams.
Local residents and police reported that some Chinese and Taiwanese nationals had been renting two hotels along the Marine Drive road for at least two months.
The suspects were presented before the Cox's Bazar Amli Court on Friday afternoon, where they were ordered to be sent to jail.
Police officials stated that raids are continuing to bring other individuals involved in this fraudulent network under legal action.
caption:
Nearly 2,000 iPhones and 40 laptops seized in a single hotel raid! 📱

Police arrested six Chinese nationals from the Hotel Sea Palace in Cox's Bazar after a raid conducted between Thursday night and Friday morning.

The operation recovered 1,938 iPhones, 40 laptops, and various communication tools, including equipment reportedly used by foreign police.

The arrests followed a tip-off from Dhaka police and a complaint filed at the Ramu police station regarding online-based fraud.

According to Ramu Police Station OC A K Fazlul Haque, the suspects were booked under the Cyber Security Act for their alleged involvement in online scams.

Local residents and police reported that some Chinese and Taiwanese nationals had been renting two hotels along the Marine Drive road for at least two months.

The suspects were presented before the Cox's Bazar Amli Court on Friday afternoon, where they were ordered to be sent to jail.

Police officials stated that raids are continuing to bring other individuals involved in this fraudulent network under legal action.

headline_marked: [[Man's body found]] on Dhaka Elevated Expressway
headline: Man's body found on Dhaka Elevated Expressway
summary: The unidentified victim, believed to be around 50, was found with his mouth taped, sparking a murder investigation.
details: Police recovered the body of an unidentified man from the Dhaka Elevated Expressway in Banani yesterday morning.
The victim, estimated to be around 50 years old, was found with his mouth taped.
He was wearing a blue outfit similar to those commonly worn by CNG-run auto-rickshaw drivers.
Banani Police Station Officer-in-Charge Faridul Islam stated that police suspect the man was murdered elsewhere and the body was dumped on the expressway.
Authorities believe the body was placed there during the night or early morning hours.
Police are currently reviewing CCTV footage from cameras installed along the expressway to identify those involved and determine how the body was transported.
Efforts are ongoing to establish the man's identity.
